annotation.title_clean: EU KIDS ACT - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy' (Proposal for a Regulation, COM(2026) 681 final)
annotation.title_en: EU KIDS ACT - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy' (Proposal for a Regulation, COM(2026) 681 final)
annotation.summary_en: European Commission proposal for an EU regulation (EU KIDS Act) protecting minors online. It sets a minimum age of 15 for autonomous accounts on social networks and video-sharing platforms, safety-by-design duties for AI companions, chatbots, games and app stores, and age-assurance rules. Enforcement builds on the DSA and AI Act. No physical or embodied AI content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Providers must not allow under-15s to create autonomous accounts on risky social networking and video-sharing services; guardians may set up limited accounts from age 13.
Safety-by-design duties for social networks, video-sharing, online games, AI companions and general conversational chatbots, including limits on addictive design and emotional dependency.
Age assurance must be accurate, privacy-preserving and non-discriminatory; self-declaration is insufficient; Member States must offer age verification solutions.
App stores must apply age-rating systems and block age-inappropriate apps for minors.
Enforcement relies on DSA and AI Act structures, with fast-track Commission proceedings and independent audits of compliance plans.
